title: (U,Th)-He dating of Pleistocene carbonates: Analytical methods and age calculations
author: Kramers, Makhubela

steps.title: Assemble furnace and sample tube
steps.instruction: Construct the furnace from standard CF UHV components as shown in Fig. 1. Insert a silica glass sample tube (10 mm outer diameter, 8 mm inner diameter) with a funnel‑shaped top of 20 mm diameter. Surround the tube with a Ni‑Cr heating coil (resistance 1 Ω m⁻¹, total length 1.5 m) that is mechanically rigid and supported only by the high‑current feedthrough base. Suspend the tube from its funnel top with a wire frame that fits snugly in the casing and can be removed after the heating assembly is taken out. Ensure Cu capsules placed in the tube have diameters ≥ 6 mm so they do not fall through.

steps.title: Install linear sliding sample magazine
steps.instruction: Fit the integrated linear sliding sample magazine: a 15 mm diameter aluminum bar drilled with vertical 8 mm diameter holes. Wrap each sample in copper foil and place it into a hole. Move the bar with external magnets while watching its position through the sapphire window to introduce samples individually.

steps.title: Prepare samples and run hot blanks
steps.instruction: Degas each silica tube in a turbo pump before use. Heat samples to approximately 950 °C (well below Cu melting point 1085 °C and well above calcination temperature ~800 °C). Maintain this temperature for about 30 min to fully calcine powdered samples and release all He. Control furnace power via a phototransistor sensor that monitors the glow through a cap over the sapphire window. Run hot blanks before each batch of samples and intersperse blanks among sample runs.

steps.title: Prepare liquid‑nitrogen cold trap
steps.instruction: Set up a cold trap with a bottom diameter of 40 mm containing 2 g activated charcoal. The large diameter prevents CO₂ snow deposited on the walls from blocking access to the charcoal layer at the bottom, where N₂, O₂ and Ar are largely adsorbed.

steps.title: Assemble extraction line and mass spectrometer
steps.instruction: Connect the extraction line (Fig. 2) using CF16 stainless‑steel tubing (internal diameter 16 mm) and all‑metal Varian‑type angle valves (labels A–F). Attach the MAP‑215‑50 single‑collector mass spectrometer (Johnston electron multiplier in analogue mode) with twin SAES AP10 getters (room temperature and 450 °C) placed in a stainless‑steel tube adjacent to the ion source, and its dedicated ion pump. Link a Dörflinger pipette (0.2 ml volume) to a 2.6 L reservoir that holds the 3He spike.

steps.title: Perform helium extraction sequence
steps.instruction: Execute the following valve and heating operations in order:

substeps.instruction: Starting condition: line under UHV, cold trap immersed in liquid nitrogen, valves B, E and F closed, A and C open.
Introduce one pipette (D) volume of the 3He spike into the line (first, with the line empty, to avoid gradual contamination of the spike reservoir).
Heat the sample for ~30 min at 950 °C.
Close valve A to trap CO₂ and adsorbed gases.
Open valve F and measure the 4He/3He ratio.
Close valves C and F, open valve E and pump the mass spectrometer with its own ion pump.
Open valves A and B, immerse the cold trap in boiling water, and pump out CO₂ and adsorbed gases with the turbo pump (pressure rises to ~10⁻³ mbar for several minutes then drops rapidly).
When pressure reaches the lower 10⁻⁸ mbar range, close valve B, open valves C and E, and re‑immerse the cold trap in liquid nitrogen to return to the starting condition.

steps.title: Calibrate 3He spike and determine amounts
steps.instruction: Calibrate the spike using a second 2.6 L reservoir:

substeps.instruction: Connect the second reservoir to the line via a calibrated Dörflinger pipette (normally used for air Ar measurements).
Evacuate the reservoir to < 10⁻⁷ mbar, then admit one pipette volume of pure natural He at recorded ambient temperature and atmospheric pressure.
With the line again under UHV, calculate the exact amount of He introduced from the reservoir via the single pipette volume.
Measure 4He/3He ratios after introducing pipette volumes of the spike and of natural He into the line; instrumental isotope fractionation cancels between calibration and sample measurements.
The calibrated spike corresponds to 1.298 × 10⁻⁶ µmol of 3He per pipette shot; subsequent runs are corrected for gradual depletion of the reservoir using an exponential decay equation.
Note that the 4He blank lies between 7 × 10⁻¹⁰ and 1.5 × 10⁻⁹ µmol, while typical sample 4He amounts range from 1 × 10⁻⁷ to 3 × 10⁻⁵ µmol, so blank corrections are usually insignificant.
